title: The Book of Numbers Timeline
sub: Forty Years in the Wilderness · A Generation Lost and Found
desc: Two censuses bookend Numbers, one generation apart — the first dies in the wilderness after refusing to trust God at Kadesh, the second stands ready on the plains of Moab, having survived Korah's rebellion, Balaam's oracles, and forty years of wandering to finally face the promised land.

eras.label: Era One · Numbers 1-2
eras.name: The First Census, and the Camp Arrangement
eras.dates: A full military census counts 603,550 fighting men by tribe, and each tribe receives a precise position around the tabernacle — Levi deliberately excluded from the count and placed at the center instead, closest to God's own dwelling.

events.title: 603,550 Fighting Men Counted
events.detail: Moses and Aaron count every Israelite male twenty years and older able to serve in the army, tribe by tribe, totaling 603,550 — with Levi deliberately excluded from the military count and assigned instead to guard the tabernacle itself.

verses.text: “The Levites must camp around the tabernacle of the testimony, so that the LORD's anger will not fall on the Israelite community. The Levites are responsible for the care of the tabernacle of the testimony.”

events.title: Twelve Tribes Arranged Around the Tabernacle
events.detail: Each tribe is assigned a specific position and marching order around the tabernacle by compass direction — Judah leading the eastern camp — with the Levites and the tent of meeting placed deliberately at the center of the whole formation.

eras.label: Era Two · Numbers 3-4
eras.name: The Levites Numbered and Assigned
eras.dates: Levi's three clans — Gershon, Kohath, and Merari — are counted separately from the rest of Israel and assigned specific tabernacle-carrying duties, with the Kohathites warned that even touching the holy furnishings directly means death.

events.title: Levi Substituted for Israel's Firstborn
events.detail: The Levites are counted from a month old and assigned to Aaron as a gift "instead of every firstborn who opens the womb" among the Israelites, with a redemption tax collected for the 273 firstborn Israelites exceeding the Levites' own number.

verses.text: “I myself have taken the Levites from among the Israelites instead of every firstborn who opens the womb among the Israelites. So the Levites belong to me, because all the firstborn are mine.”

events.title: Carrying the Tabernacle — Kohath, Gershon, and Merari
events.detail: Working-age Levites (thirty to fifty) receive precisely assigned carrying duties for the journey — the Kohathites bearing the sanctuary's holiest furnishings only after Aaron's sons have covered them, under strict warning that touching or even viewing the uncovered holy things directly means death.

verses.text: “When Aaron and his sons have finished covering the sanctuary and all the furnishings of the sanctuary… then the Kohathites will come to carry them; but they must not touch any holy thing, or they will die.”

eras.label: Era Three · Numbers 5-6
eras.name: Purity Laws, the Test for Jealousy, and the Nazirite Vow
eras.dates: Camp purity laws, a ritual ordeal for a husband's unproven suspicion of his wife, and the voluntary Nazirite vow of separation all precede the priestly blessing that closes with God's own name placed directly on Israel.

events.title: Camp Purity, and the Ordeal of Jealousy
events.detail: Ceremonially unclean people are sent outside the camp to protect the tabernacle's purity, and a ritual involving "bitter water that brings a curse" resolves cases where a husband suspects his wife of unfaithfulness without proof — a woman genuinely innocent suffers no harm from drinking it.

events.title: The Nazirite Vow — Voluntary Separation to God
events.detail: Anyone, man or woman, may take a Nazirite vow of special consecration involving abstinence from wine, uncut hair, and avoiding contact with the dead — a temporary, voluntary holiness available to any Israelite, not only priests.

events.title: The Priestly Blessing — God's Name Placed on Israel
events.detail: God gives Aaron the precise words for blessing Israel — a threefold benediction of protection, grace, and peace — explaining that through it the priests "put my name on the Israelites," and God himself will bless them.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] bless you and protect you; the LORD [Yahweh] make his face to shine upon you, and be gracious to you; the LORD [Yahweh] lift up his countenance upon you and give you peace.”

eras.label: Era Four · Numbers 7
eras.name: The Leaders' Dedication Gifts
eras.dates: Twelve tribal leaders bring identical, lavish dedication gifts for the newly anointed altar — one leader per day for twelve straight days — a deliberately repetitive chapter that treats every tribe's generosity as equally significant.

events.title: Twelve Days, Twelve Identical Offerings
events.detail: Each of Israel's twelve tribal leaders brings an identical set of silver vessels, gold incense, and sacrificial animals to dedicate the altar over twelve consecutive days — an intentionally repetitive record that gives every tribe equal weight and honor, closing with Moses hearing the LORD's voice from between the cherubim.

verses.text: “When Moses went into the tent of meeting to speak with the LORD, he heard the voice speaking to him from above the atonement lid that was on the ark of the testimony, from between the two cherubim.”

eras.label: Era Five · Numbers 8
eras.name: The Levites Purified and Set Apart
eras.dates: A wave-offering ceremony formally consecrates the Levites for tabernacle service, with a defined career span — beginning duty at twenty-five and retiring from active labor at fifty.

events.title: The Levites Dedicated as a Wave Offering
events.detail: The Israelites lay hands on the Levites before the LORD, who accepts them "as a wave offering" in place of Israel's firstborn sons, purified and set apart specifically to protect the rest of the nation from the danger of approaching the sanctuary directly.

verses.text: “I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and his sons from among the Israelites, to do the work for the Israelites in the tent of meeting, and to make atonement for the Israelites, so there will be no plague among the Israelites when the Israelites come near the sanctuary.”

eras.label: Era Six · Numbers 9
eras.name: The Second Passover, and the Cloud of Guidance
eras.dates: A provision for those unable to keep Passover on schedule due to ritual uncleanness establishes a makeup date a month later, and the cloud over the tabernacle becomes Israel's literal navigation system for the whole wilderness journey.

events.title: A Second Chance to Keep the Passover
events.detail: Men defiled by contact with a corpse ask why they should be excluded from Passover, and God provides a makeup date exactly one month later — extending the same provision to any resident foreigner who wishes to observe it.

verses.text: “If any of you or of your posterity become ceremonially defiled by touching a dead body, or are on a journey far away, then he may observe the Passover to the LORD. They may observe it on the fourteenth day of the second month.”

events.title: The Cloud That Governed Every Move
events.detail: A cloud covers the tabernacle by day and appears as fire by night, and Israel's entire travel schedule depends on it completely — camping for as long as the cloud rests, moving the instant it lifts, whether for two days or an entire year.

verses.text: “Whether it was for two days, or a month, or a year that the cloud prolonged its stay over the tabernacle, the Israelites remained camped without traveling; but when it was taken up, they traveled on. At the commandment of the LORD they camped, and at the commandment of the LORD they traveled on.”

eras.label: Era Seven · Numbers 10
eras.name: The Silver Trumpets, and Israel Sets Out
eras.dates: Two silver trumpets coordinate the massive camp's movements and assemblies, and the cloud finally lifts from Sinai — sending Israel on its first march since arriving nearly a year earlier, with Moses's own traveling prayer marking the ark's every move.

events.title: Trumpets for Assembly, Alarm, and War
events.detail: Two hammered silver trumpets are made for distinct signals — assembling the whole community, summoning only the leaders, or sounding the alarm for war or festival — becoming "an eternal ordinance throughout your generations."

events.title: "Rise Up, O LORD!" — the March Begins
events.detail: Nearly a year after arriving at Sinai, the cloud lifts and Israel sets out in precise tribal order toward the wilderness of Paran; Moses's own prayer marks the ark's movement at the front of the march — "Rise up, O LORD! May your enemies be scattered" — and rest at each stop.

verses.text: “When the ark traveled, Moses would say, ‘Rise up, O LORD! May your enemies be scattered, and may those who hate you flee before you!’ And when it came to rest he would say, ‘Return, O LORD, to the many thousands of Israel!’”

eras.label: Era Eight · Numbers 11
eras.name: Complaining, Quail, and the Seventy Elders
eras.dates: Nostalgia for Egyptian food turns into open weeping over manna, and God's response is twofold — quail delivered in such excess it becomes a plague, and seventy elders who share Moses's prophetic burden so he no longer carries the nation alone.

events.title: "If Only We Had Meat to Eat!"
events.detail: Complaints about the monotony of manna and nostalgia for Egyptian food provoke the LORD's anger and burn part of the camp; Moses, overwhelmed by the people's weeping, complains to God that the burden of leading them alone is too heavy to bear.

verses.text: “I am not able to bear this entire people alone, because it is too heavy for me! But if you are going to deal with me like this, then kill me immediately.”

events.title: The Seventy Elders, and Quail Until It Comes Out Their Nostrils
events.detail: God distributes some of the Spirit resting on Moses to seventy elders to share the burden of leadership, while a wind-driven abundance of quail — so much it becomes sickening rather than satisfying — falls on the very people still chewing it when a plague strikes them at Kibroth Hattaavah, "the graves of craving."

verses.text: “Moses said to him, ‘Are you jealous for me? I wish that all the LORD's [Yahweh] people were prophets, that the LORD [Yahweh] would put his Spirit on them!’”

eras.label: Era Nine · Numbers 12
eras.name: Miriam and Aaron Challenge Moses
eras.dates: Miriam and Aaron's complaint about Moses's marriage becomes a challenge to his unique authority, and God's direct comparison — every prophet gets visions and dreams, but Moses gets to see God's own form face to face — leaves Miriam struck with a skin disease as consequence.

events.title: "With Him I Will Speak Face to Face"
events.detail: Miriam and Aaron's complaint about Moses's Cushite wife reveals a deeper challenge to his unique authority as prophet; God directly defends Moses as uniquely faithful, speaking to him "face to face" rather than through visions, and Miriam alone is struck with a skin disease for seven days as a consequence.

verses.text: “If there is a prophet among you, I the LORD [Yahweh] will make myself known to him in a vision… My servant Moses is not like this; he is faithful in all my house. With him I will speak face to face, openly and not in riddles, and he will see the form of the LORD [Yahweh].”

eras.label: Era Ten · Numbers 13
eras.name: The Twelve Spies
eras.dates: Twelve tribal representatives scout Canaan for forty days and return with the same evidence — a genuinely fruitful land — but ten interpret the fortified cities and giant inhabitants as an insurmountable threat while only Caleb dares to say Israel can take it.

events.title: "We Seemed Like Grasshoppers"
events.detail: Twelve spies, one from each tribe, scout Canaan for forty days and bring back genuine evidence of the land's fruitfulness, but ten of them frame the fortified cities and the giant-descended Anakites as unconquerable, while Caleb alone insists "we are well able to conquer it."

verses.text: “Then Caleb silenced the people before Moses, saying, ‘Let us go up and occupy it, for we are well able to conquer it.’”
“We even saw the Nephilim there… and we seemed like grasshoppers both to ourselves and to them.”

eras.label: Era Eleven · Numbers 14
eras.name: Israel's Rebellion and the Forty Years' Sentence
eras.dates: The people's terrified response to the spies' report escalates into open rebellion and a plan to return to Egypt, and only Moses's direct intercession — appealing to God's own revealed character — spares the nation from immediate destruction, though an entire generation is still sentenced to die in the wilderness.

events.title: "Forgive the Iniquity of This People"
events.detail: The community weeps, threatens to stone Joshua and Caleb, and plans to appoint a new leader back to Egypt; Moses intercedes directly, appealing to God's own self-description as "slow to anger and abounding in loyal love" to plead for forgiveness rather than annihilation.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] is slow to anger and abounding in loyal love, forgiving iniquity and transgression, but by no means clearing the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children until the third and fourth generations.”

events.title: A Generation Sentenced to Forty Years
events.detail: God forgives the nation from destruction but sentences the unbelieving generation — everyone twenty and older except Caleb and Joshua — to forty years of wandering, one year for each day the spies scouted the land; a hasty, unauthorized attempt to invade anyway ends in defeat.

verses.text: “As I live, all the earth will be filled with the glory of the LORD [Yahweh].”

eras.label: Era Twelve · Numbers 15
eras.name: Offerings, a Sabbath-Breaker, and Tassels
eras.dates: Even mid-judgment, God gives instructions for offerings in the land Israel will eventually enter, before a real incident — a man gathering wood on the Sabbath — forces a ruling, and tassels on every garment corner become a permanent visual reminder to obey.

events.title: Offerings for the Land Ahead, and Forgiveness for the Unintentional
events.detail: Even under judgment, God gives forward-looking instructions for offerings once Israel enters the land, distinguishing unintentional sin (which receives atonement and forgiveness) from defiant, deliberate rebellion, which "must be completely cut off."

events.title: A Man Stoned for Gathering Wood on the Sabbath
events.detail: A man caught gathering wood on the Sabbath is held in custody until the LORD gives a direct ruling — death by stoning — carried out by the whole community outside the camp.

events.title: Blue Tassels as a Reminder
events.detail: God commands blue-threaded tassels on every garment corner so that looking at them will remind Israel to "obey all my commandments" rather than follow "your own heart and your own eyes."

verses.text: “You must have this tassel so that you may look at it and remember all the commandments of the LORD and obey them and so that you do not follow after your own heart and your own eyes that lead you to unfaithfulness.”

eras.label: Era Thirteen · Numbers 16
eras.name: Korah's Rebellion
eras.dates: A Levite and two Reubenite leaders challenge Moses and Aaron's unique authority with 250 followers, and the earth itself opens to swallow the ringleaders alive — followed immediately by a deadly plague that only Aaron's emergency intercession stops. (Hebrew chapter 16 covers what most English Bibles print as 16:1-35.)

events.title: "You Take Too Much Upon Yourselves"
events.detail: Korah the Levite, joined by Dathan and Abiram and 250 respected leaders, challenges Moses and Aaron's authority, claiming the whole community is equally holy; Moses proposes a direct test before the LORD using censers of incense.

verses.text: “They assembled against Moses and Aaron, saying to them, ‘You take too much upon yourselves, seeing that the whole community is holy, every one of them, and the LORD is among them. Why then do you exalt yourselves above the community of the LORD?’”

events.title: The Earth Opens, and Fire Consumes 250 Men
events.detail: The ground splits open and swallows Korah, Dathan, and Abiram alive along with their households, while fire from the LORD consumes the 250 men who offered incense — a sign so total that Moses warns it proves the LORD, not Moses, had sent him all along.

verses.text: “The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, along with their households, and all Korah's men, and all their goods. They and all that they had went down alive into the pit, and the earth closed over them.”

eras.label: Era Fourteen · Numbers 17
eras.name: Aaron's Budding Staff
eras.dates: Still shaken by Korah's judgment, the people murmur again — and God settles the question of legitimate priesthood for good with a sign no one could fake: overnight, Aaron's staff alone sprouts buds, blossoms, and ripe almonds. (Hebrew chapter 17 covers what most English Bibles number as 16:36-17:13.)

events.title: One Staff Blossoms Overnight
events.detail: Twelve staffs, one per tribal leader, are placed before the ark overnight; only Aaron's staff for the tribe of Levi sprouts buds, blossoms, and ripe almonds by morning — settling the question of legitimate priesthood and becoming a permanent sign preserved before the testimony to end further complaints. (Numbered 16:36-17:13 in most English translations.)

verses.text: “On the next day Moses went into the tent of the testimony — and the staff of Aaron for the house of Levi had sprouted, and brought forth buds, and produced blossoms, and yielded almonds!”

eras.label: Era Fifteen · Numbers 18
eras.name: Priestly and Levitical Portions
eras.dates: The LORD explains exactly how priests and Levites will be supported without owning land — the priests' share of every offering, and the Levites' entire inheritance drawn from Israel's tithes instead of territory.

events.title: "I Am Your Portion and Your Inheritance"
events.detail: Aaron and his sons receive detailed rights to specific portions of every offering as their livelihood, while the Levites receive the nation's tithes as their entire inheritance in place of land — because, as God tells Aaron directly, "I am your portion and your inheritance among the Israelites."

verses.text: “The LORD spoke to Aaron, ‘You will have no inheritance in their land, nor will you have any portion of property among them — I am your portion and your inheritance among the Israelites.’”

eras.label: Era Sixteen · Numbers 19
eras.name: The Red Heifer
eras.dates: A uniquely paradoxical ritual — the ashes of a burned red heifer purify anyone defiled by contact with death, even while the ritual itself renders every person who handles it temporarily unclean.

events.title: Ashes That Purify the Defiled
events.detail: A flawless red heifer is burned entirely outside the camp, and its ashes, mixed with water, become the required purification for anyone who has touched a corpse — a ritual so paradoxical that it defiles the priest who performs it even as it cleanses everyone else.

eras.label: Era Seventeen · Numbers 20
eras.name: Water From the Rock, and the Deaths of Miriam and Aaron
eras.dates: Nearly forty years after a similar crisis in Exodus, thirst provokes rebellion again — but this time Moses strikes the rock in anger rather than simply speaking to it, and the consequence is severe: neither he nor Aaron will enter the promised land.

events.title: Miriam Dies at Kadesh
events.detail: Miriam dies and is buried at Kadesh, marking the close of the original wilderness generation's leadership trio.

events.title: "You Did Not Trust Me Enough" — Moses Strikes the Rock
events.detail: Facing another water crisis, Moses is told to speak to the rock, but instead strikes it twice in anger before an audience he calls "rebels" — water still flows, but God declares that because Moses failed to treat him as holy before the people, neither he nor Aaron will enter the promised land.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] said to Moses and to Aaron, ‘Because you did not trust me enough to show me as holy before the Israelites, therefore you will not bring this community into the land I have given them.’”

events.title: Edom Refuses Passage, and Aaron Dies on Mount Hor
events.detail: Edom refuses Israel safe passage through its territory despite a peaceful, careful request, forcing a detour; Aaron dies on Mount Hor after his priestly garments are transferred to his son Eleazar, and the whole nation mourns him for thirty days.

eras.label: Era Eighteen · Numbers 21
eras.name: The Bronze Serpent, and Victories Over Sihon and Og
eras.dates: Venomous snakes sent as judgment for renewed complaining are answered with a strange cure — a bronze serpent lifted on a pole — before Israel finally wins real military victories, defeating two Amorite kings and taking their territory.

events.title: "Look at the Bronze Snake and Live"
events.detail: Renewed complaints about the wilderness diet bring venomous snakes among the people; when they repent, Moses is told to mount a bronze snake on a pole so that anyone bitten who looks at it will live — a strange remedy later invoked by Jesus as an image of his own crucifixion.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] said to Moses, ‘Make a poisonous snake and set it on a pole. When anyone who is bitten looks at it, he will live.’ So Moses made a bronze snake and put it on a pole… when he looked at the bronze snake he lived.”

events.title: Sihon and Og Defeated
events.detail: After Sihon of the Amorites refuses safe passage and attacks, Israel defeats him decisively and takes his territory, then does the same to King Og of Bashan — Israel's first substantial territorial conquests east of the Jordan.

eras.label: Era Nineteen · Numbers 22
eras.name: Balaam and the Talking Donkey
eras.dates: Terrified by Israel's advance, Moab's king hires a foreign diviner to curse Israel, but God repeatedly overrules Balaam's intentions — most memorably through his own donkey, which sees the angel of the LORD before Balaam does and is given a voice to say so.

events.title: Balak Hires Balaam to Curse Israel
events.detail: Terrified by Israel's approach, King Balak of Moab hires the diviner Balaam to curse them; God initially forbids Balaam from going, but permits it on the second request, on the strict condition that Balaam speak only what God tells him.

verses.text: “God said to Balaam, ‘You must not go with them; you must not curse the people, for they are blessed.’”

events.title: The Donkey That Saw the Angel First
events.detail: The angel of the LORD blocks the road with a drawn sword, visible to Balaam's donkey but not to Balaam himself; after the donkey balks three times and is beaten each time, the LORD opens its mouth to protest the treatment, and only then does Balaam's own eyes open to see the angel standing before him.

verses.text: “Then the LORD opened the mouth of the donkey, and she said to Balaam, ‘What have I done to you that you have beaten me these three times?’”

eras.label: Era Twenty · Numbers 23-24
eras.name: Balaam's Oracles
eras.dates: Across four separate attempts, Balak keeps relocating Balaam to a new vantage point hoping for a different result, but Balaam can only speak the blessings God puts in his mouth — including a striking messianic image of a star rising out of Jacob.

events.title: "How Can I Curse One Whom God Has Not Cursed?"
events.detail: Balaam delivers two oracles blessing rather than cursing Israel despite Balak's mounting frustration and repeated attempts to change the outcome by relocating him, insisting each time that he can only speak what the LORD puts in his mouth.

verses.text: “God is not a man, that he should lie, nor a human being, that he should change his mind. Has he said, and will he not do it? Or has he spoken, and will he not make it happen?”

events.title: "A Star Will March Forth Out of Jacob"
events.detail: Balaam's final two oracles bless Israel even more emphatically, including a striking prophecy of a future ruler — "a star will march forth out of Jacob, and a scepter will rise out of Israel" — provoking Balak's fury before Balaam returns home unpaid and uncompromised.

verses.text: “I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not close at hand. A star will march forth out of Jacob, and a scepter will rise out of Israel.”

eras.label: Era Twenty-One · Numbers 25
eras.name: Baal Peor and Phinehas's Zeal
eras.dates: Where Balaam's curses failed, Moabite seduction into idolatry nearly succeeds — a plague breaks out that only stops when the priest Phinehas takes direct, violent action against a flagrant public offense.

events.title: Phinehas Stops the Plague
events.detail: Israelite men are drawn into sexual immorality and idol worship with Moabite women at Baal Peor, provoking a deadly plague; Phinehas, grandson of Aaron, kills an Israelite man and Midianite woman in the act, stopping the plague and earning God's "covenant of peace" and a permanent priestly line for his zeal. (Verse 19's brief transitional clause is attached to most English Bibles' 26:1.)

verses.text: “Phinehas son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, has turned my anger away from the Israelites, when he manifested such zeal for my sake among them, so that I did not consume the Israelites in my zeal.”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Two · Numbers 26
eras.name: The Second Census
eras.dates: A new generation is counted on the plains of Moab, and the total — 601,730 — comes in nearly identical to the first census, but belongs to an entirely different set of men: not one survivor of the first count remains except Caleb and Joshua.

events.title: A New Generation Counted
events.detail: As the wilderness generation finally dies out, a second census counts the new generation by tribe and family, closing with the stark note that not a single man survives from the first census taken at Sinai — except Caleb and Joshua, the two who trusted God at Kadesh.

verses.text: “The LORD had said of them, ‘They will surely die in the wilderness.’ And there was not left a single man of them, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Three · Numbers 27
eras.name: Zelophehad's Daughters, and Joshua Commissioned
eras.dates: Five sisters with no brothers successfully petition for the right to inherit their father's land, reshaping Israel's inheritance law — and Moses, told he will die without entering Canaan, formally hands leadership to Joshua.

events.title: Five Daughters Change the Inheritance Law
events.detail: Zelophehad's five daughters petition Moses directly, arguing their father's name should not disappear just because he had no sons; God rules in their favor, establishing a permanent legal principle for daughters to inherit when there is no son.

events.title: "So That the Community May Not Be Like Sheep Without a Shepherd"
events.detail: Told he will see the promised land but not enter it, Moses asks God to appoint a successor rather than leave Israel leaderless; God chooses Joshua, and Moses publicly commissions him before Eleazar the priest and the whole community, laying hands on him and transferring some of his authority.

verses.text: “Moses spoke to the LORD: ‘Let the LORD [Yahweh], the God [Elohim] of the spirits of all humankind, appoint a man over the community, who will go out before them, and who will come in before them… so that the community of the LORD [Yahweh] may not be like sheep that have no shepherd.’”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Four · Numbers 28-29
eras.name: The Calendar of Offerings
eras.dates: A comprehensive sacrificial calendar spells out the exact offerings required for every day, Sabbath, new moon, and annual feast — a level of detail matched by real specificity about who is expected to keep track. (Hebrew chapter 30 begins at what most English Bibles number as 29:40.)

events.title: Daily, Sabbath, and Monthly Offerings
events.detail: God specifies the continual daily burnt offering, additional Sabbath offerings, and monthly new-moon sacrifices, then details the offerings for Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread.

events.title: The Autumn Festivals — Trumpets, Atonement, and Shelters
events.detail: The autumn calendar specifies offerings for the Feast of Trumpets, the Day of Atonement, and the seven-day Feast of Shelters — whose bull offerings deliberately decrease by one each day, from thirteen down to seven, across the festival week.

eras.label: Era Twenty-Five · Numbers 30
eras.name: Laws on Vows
eras.dates: Detailed law governs when a vow made by an unmarried daughter or a wife can be overruled by her father or husband — and when it stands permanently, as for a widow or divorced woman answerable to no one else. (Hebrew chapter 30 covers what most English Bibles number as 29:40-30:16.)

events.title: When a Vow Stands, and When It Can Be Nullified
events.detail: A man's vow is always binding, but a young woman's or wife's vow can be nullified by her father or husband if he objects the same day he hears of it — while a widow or divorced woman's vow always stands, since no one else bears responsibility for it. (Numbered 29:40-30:16 in most English translations.)

eras.label: Era Twenty-Six · Numbers 31
eras.name: War Against Midian
eras.dates: A punitive campaign against Midian for its role in the Baal Peor seduction ends in total victory, an extensive division of plunder between soldiers and the wider community, and a tribute set aside specifically for the LORD.

events.title: Vengeance on Midian
events.detail: Twelve thousand Israelite troops defeat Midian completely, killing every male including Balaam himself; Moses is angered that the women — responsible for Israel's seduction into idolatry at Peor — were initially spared, and detailed rules distribute the resulting plunder between the army, the community, and a tribute set apart for the LORD.

verses.text: “These people through the counsel of Balaam caused the Israelites to act treacherously against the LORD in the matter of Peor — which resulted in the plague among the community of the LORD!”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Seven · Numbers 32
eras.name: Reuben, Gad, and Half-Manasseh Settle East of the Jordan
eras.dates: Two and a half tribes request the already-conquered land east of the Jordan for their large herds, provoking Moses's fear of a repeat of the spies' failure — resolved only by their pledge to fight alongside their brothers until every tribe has its inheritance.

events.title: "Must Your Brothers Go to War While You Remain Here?"
events.detail: Reuben and Gad, with large herds, request the fertile land already conquered east of the Jordan instead of crossing into Canaan; Moses initially fears a repeat of the unbelief that doomed the previous generation, but grants the request once they pledge to fight alongside the other tribes until the conquest is complete.

verses.text: “Moses said to the Gadites and the Reubenites, ‘Must your brothers go to war while you remain here?’”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Eight · Numbers 33
eras.name: The Wilderness Itinerary
eras.dates: A complete travel log records every campsite of the forty-year journey from Egypt to the plains of Moab, before God issues a stark warning about what happens if Israel fails to fully drive out Canaan's inhabitants.

events.title: Forty Years, Camp by Camp
events.detail: A comprehensive itinerary records every stop of Israel's wilderness journey from Rameses to the plains of Moab, including the dates of Aaron's death on Mount Hor at 123 years old.

events.title: "Thorns in Your Side" — a Warning About Incomplete Conquest
events.detail: God commands the complete removal of Canaan's inhabitants and their idols, warning that anyone left in the land will become "irritants in your eyes and thorns in your side" — and that whatever Israel fails to do to them, God will do to Israel instead.

verses.text: “If you do not drive out the inhabitants of the land before you, then those whom you allow to remain will be irritants in your eyes and thorns in your side, and will cause you trouble in the land where you will be living.”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Nine · Numbers 34
eras.name: The Land's Boundaries
eras.dates: Precise geographic borders define the promised land itself, and named leaders from each of the remaining tribes are appointed to oversee its fair division once Israel finally crosses in.

events.title: Israel's Borders, and the Men Who Will Divide the Land
events.detail: God specifies Canaan's exact southern, western, northern, and eastern boundaries, then names Eleazar, Joshua, and one leader from each remaining tribe to oversee the land's fair distribution by lot.

eras.label: Era Thirty · Numbers 35
eras.name: Levitical Cities and Cities of Refuge
eras.dates: Forty-eight cities scattered through the other tribes' territory become the Levites' inheritance, and six of them are set apart specifically as cities of refuge — protecting an accidental killer from vengeance until a fair trial, and after it, until the high priest's own death.

events.title: Forty-Eight Cities for the Levites
events.detail: The Levites, owning no territory of their own, receive forty-eight cities with surrounding grazing land carved out of every other tribe's inheritance, six of them designated as cities of refuge for anyone who kills accidentally.

events.title: Refuge Until the High Priest's Death
events.detail: Detailed law distinguishes intentional murder, which demands death, from accidental killing, which grants refuge and protection from the "avenger of blood" — but only until a fair community trial, and afterward only until the reigning high priest himself dies, since "blood defiles the land" and cannot otherwise be cleansed.

verses.text: “You must not pollute the land where you live, for blood defiles the land, and the land cannot be cleansed of the blood that is shed there, except by the blood of the person who shed it.”

eras.label: Era Thirty-One · Numbers 36
eras.name: Zelophehad's Daughters Marry Within Their Tribe
eras.dates: The book's final chapter closes a loose end from chapter 27 — a practical amendment ensuring Zelophehad's inheriting daughters marry within their own tribe, so no family's land permanently transfers to another tribe through marriage.

events.title: Keeping the Inheritance Within the Tribe
events.detail: Concerned that Zelophehad's daughters might marry outside their tribe and permanently transfer their inherited land elsewhere, tribal leaders raise the issue with Moses, who rules that the daughters may marry whomever they choose, provided it is within their father's own tribe — and the book of Numbers closes with the daughters doing exactly that.
